title: From DM to revenue.
description: The cold DM that turned a stranger into a six figure yes, annotated line by line.
kicker: One DM · a six figure yes
formHeader: One DM to a stranger, and a six figure yes that started with a reply thirty minutes later.
formEyebrow: Get it free, in your inbox

blocks.text: I sent one cold message to a founder I'd never met. He replied in thirty minutes, and that message is the reason I'm his business partner today.
Everyone asks what the message said, which is the wrong question.
The writing wasn't especially clever. It worked because it did the thing it was selling, to the person who'd be buying it.

Alec had posted about growing his company. I read his last twenty posts before I wrote a word, to learn how he talks rather than to flatter him, and then I wrote to him in his own language. In the second line I told him I'd found him the same way I'd find his future customers, so the pitch arrived as outreach, in his inbox, while he was reading it.

After that came three facts in a deliberate order: a business I'd run at eighteen, outreach I'd already done for someone with 85,000 followers (numbers attached), and my current job with its honest limit, afternoons and weekends only. That last one is a weakness, and it's what made the other two believable.
Doing the work in the message itself does two things:

items: It answers the only question that matters before anyone asks it. A founder reading a cold pitch wants to know whether you can actually do the thing, and landing in his inbox is the answer.
Nobody can fake it. Anyone can say they're good at outreach; almost nobody will find you, read you and write something you haven't already seen twice that week.

blocks.text: The same structure turns a cold DM into a customer, a partnership or an investor call. Only the ask changes. You do a piece of the work before anyone agrees to pay you for it, and you put that work inside the message.

Put your email in and I'll send you the message itself, annotated: what I knew about him before I wrote a word, why every line is there, what he wrote back, and the structure you can run on anyone you need a yes from.

disclosure: You will also get The Draft, one letter a week on B2B social and content strategy. Leave whenever you like.
